name: card
title: Card
purpose: One section of a view set apart by a border or a background shift, with an optional title, one quiet action and a body.
whenToUse: Sparingly. Content sits on the page by default, under a heading. Reach for a card only when grouping helps: a set of facts with an action that applies to all of them, or a region that must read as separate from the content around it.
For one or two sections of a view that hold different things, each laid out by what it holds.
With the sunken variant for a quieter region inside a bordered layout, where a second border would be noise.
whenNotToUse: For each of several similar items. A list of similar items is a list, not a card grid: use the list or the data table. Three or more sibling cards with the same structure fail the identical-card-grid rule.
Inside another card. Use one card and separate what is inside it with a heading or a divider. A nested card fails the nested-cards rule.
As the frame of a whole view, or around every section of it. Use headings and spacing on the page.
For a request that waits for an answer. Use the approval.
For a message about the view. Use an alert.
For content that floats above the page. Only an overlay takes a shadow, and a card never does.

variants.name: bordered
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. A 1px border on the raised surface.

variants.name: sunken
variants.use: A background shift with no border. Keep quiet, muted text out of it: the muted colour does not reach 4.5:1 on the sunken surface in the light theme.

accessibility: Use a section with aria-labelledby pointing at ds-card__title when the card has a title, so it is a named region. Give each card on a view a different title. Use a div for a card with no title.

ds-card__title is a heading. Its level is the one under the heading it sits beneath: h2 directly under the view's h1, h3 inside a section headed by an h2. In a queue or a list every title takes the same level. The class sets the size, so the level changes nothing on screen. It is drawn at the size of body text whatever its level.

The header holds at most one action, in ds-card__action: a small quiet button or a link with the same classes. It is never primary. When several cards carry the same words, add an aria-label that starts with those words and names the card.
The header is 44px tall, so the small button's padded pointer target stays inside it.
A card is not focusable and takes no press. To make something pressable, put a link or a button inside it.
